inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, Section VIII note XIV.2 (3750.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:14311): total equity-settled share-based payment expense for FY2025 was a net REVERSAL of RMB -82.5m (forfeitures exceeded new vesting); floored at 0 for FY0. H1 FY2026 interim note (3750.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:11010) shows RMB 184.8m, i.e. ~0.07% of revenue. No equity-award cash taxes disclosed. SBC is immaterial: the explicit SBC row is kept at 0% and house/street coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: Treasury-share purchases of RMB 1.55bn in H1 FY2025 relate to restricted-share plan obligations, not a capital-return programme; recorded as 0 for valuation purposes. The flat count is a modelling convention CATL does not pay for via buybacks; with SBC at ~0.07% of revenue the omission is immaterial.
inputs.share_count_basis: Share capital on issue at 30 Sep 2026: 4,627.25m shares (3750.HK_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:591, share capital RMB 4,627,250 thousand at RMB1 par), A-shares + H-shares, including unvested restricted shares already issued. The Metrics CSV carries 4,598.7m for Q3 FY2026 (ex-treasury); the larger issued figure is used as the fully diluted count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed (at 0%) in the flows; there is no non-SBC issuance pending after the May-2025 H-share IPO.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1735, Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-22T12:38:26Z. Statements and all flows are in RMB (CSV in CNY millions); H-shares quote in HKD on HKEX. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1735 for the HKD canonical figures. Parity check against the Shenzhen A-share (300750.SZ, CNY 220.41 at 2026-10-22T07:04Z): 220.41 x 1.1735 = HKD 258.6 vs the H-share at HKD 338.4 -- the H-share trades at a ~31% PREMIUM to the A-share (an unusual, persistent feature of this dual listing since the May-2025 HKEX IPO, driven by international-investor access and the H-share's inclusion in global indices). The direction of the rate is confirmed by the 52-week ranges (H 336-794 HKD vs A 218-469 CNY, ratio ~1.5-1.7 both ends); the gap is a listing premium, not an FX error. The CNY-denominated twins (weighted_iv_cny etc.) are directly comparable to the A-share price.
inputs.price_note: HKEX regular close (16:08 HKT). 52-week range HKD 336.0-794.5; the price is at the bottom of the range, down ~57% from the high, after three consecutive quarters of gross-margin compression (26.3% FY2025 -> 23.9% H1 FY2026 -> 20.7% Q3 FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_note: Cash & cash equivalents RMB 333,397.6m (Q3 FY2026 cash-flow statement closing balance, 3750.HK_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:841; balance-sheet 'cash at bank and on hand' is RMB 369,813.8m, the ~RMB 36.4bn difference being restricted deposits backing bank-acceptance notes payable, left out as it funds an operating liability). Total debt RMB 185,861.2m = short-term borrowings 39,897.6 + non-current liabilities due within one year 16,871.1 + long-term borrowings 76,354.8 + bonds payable 52,737.7 (Q3 FY2026 balance sheet lines 540/563/576/577); excludes lease liabilities, which are bridged separately. Net cash RMB 147.5bn is ~1.8x the FY0 owner-FCF base, so interest income (RMB 10.6bn FY2025) is stripped from the flows and the cash pile added once in the bridge. Debt rose RMB 69bn during 9M FY2026 (new RMB 50bn medium-term notes) while cash also rose; the bridge uses the 30 Sep 2026 figures for both.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% risk-free; 6.0% mature-market ERP plus ~1.0% China country/governance premium; equity beta ~1.1 for a scaled, net-cash but cyclical and policy-exposed manufacturer -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Net cash of RMB 147.5bn means the enterprise is unlevered in economic terms, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.5%. The same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios: margin, price-war, geopolitical and cyclical risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS-16/CAS-21 lease liabilities (RMB 4,064.9m non-current at 30 Sep 2026 plus ~RMB 479m current, the FY2025 figure as Q3 does not split it) are deducted once in the equity bridge; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows and D&A includes right-of-use depreciation (RMB 337m FY2025). Leases are 2.4% of borrowings and immaterial to the result either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once via the leakage driver. Non-controlling interests took RMB 4,585m of FY2025 net profit (6.0% of total net profit of RMB 76,786m; NCI book RMB 33.9bn). Rather than deduct the NCI stock in the bridge, the cash_tax_rate_path is a combined tax-plus-NCI leakage rate: FY2025 effective income tax 14.2% (HNTE 15% rate) -> 15%, combined with 6% NCI leakage gives 1 - 0.85 x 0.94 = 20.1%, rounded to 20%, drifting to 21% as overseas (Hungary/Spain/Indonesia) profits grow. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT (EBITDA 108,602 - D&A 26,937 = 81,666) x (1 - 0.20) = 65.3bn vs attributable net income 72,201 less after-tax net interest income (10,595 - 2,734) x 0.85 = 6.7bn -> 65.5bn; ties within 0.3%.
inputs.ebitda_definition: CSV EBITDA = profit before tax + interest expense - interest income + D&A (FY2025: 89,526.5 + 2,734.0 - 10,594.7 + 26,936.7 = 108,602.5, 25.6% of revenue). It therefore INCLUDES other income (government grants RMB 10.6bn), share of profits of associates/JVs (RMB 7.35bn), fair-value gains (RMB 0.97bn) and asset impairments (RMB -8.66bn, mostly inventory write-downs, a recurring cost in a deflating battery-price environment). Associates' income is kept in the flows and the RMB 72.8bn of long-term equity investments is therefore NOT added in the bridge (matching-asset rule, one or the other). The RMB 62.8bn of financial assets held for trading (structured deposits / wealth-management products, Q3 FY2026 line 478) IS added in the bridge; its P&L return is the ~RMB 1bn fair-value gain (0.23% of FY2025 revenue), which is removed by rounding the year-1 EBITDA margin down 0.2pp (22.0% run-rate -> 21.8%).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US/cyclical adaptations applied: currency-matched WACC, CNY/HKD bridge, leases-as-debt, NCI via leakage, trading assets bridged). FRESH BUILD -- first valuation of this ticker; no prior Drivers/DCF file and no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 of the forecast is FY2026, of which 9 months are reported: 9M revenue RMB 442.1bn (+56% YoY) and Q3 EBITDA margin ~19.7% (derived: Q3 PBT 25,261 + interest expense 1,137 - interest income 2,525 + est. D&A 8,750). The year-1 drivers are therefore mostly actuals: FY2026E revenue ~RMB 623bn (+47%) assumes a Q4 of ~RMB 180bn vs Q3's 165bn, and FY2026E EBITDA of ~RMB 136bn (H1 68.1 + Q3 ~32.6 + Q4 ~36) is a 21.8% margin. The 2026 margin compression is treated as a real re-basing, not noise: much of 2026's revenue growth is raw-material (copper, electrolyte, lithium) cost pass-through at a lag, which inflates revenue while unit profit per Wh (~RMB 0.11) holds, so percentage margins fall mechanically and the base case does NOT recover to FY2025's 25.6% EBITDA margin; it holds ~20.5-21%, the lower half of the FY2022-FY2025 range (FY2022 GM 20.3%). Working capital: CATL runs structurally negative working capital (payables + notes payable RMB 333bn vs receivables + receivables financing + inventory RMB 284bn at Q3 FY2026) so growth has historically released cash (+RMB 33bn in FY2025), but 9M FY2026 reversed that (-RMB 25bn as inventory and receivables outgrew payables); base case takes no credit (wc_capture 0%), bull takes 8%, bear charges -5%. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical manufacturer, not the 20x compounder default). SBC immaterial (<0.1% of revenue) so band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a.
inputs.owner_fcf_fy0_build: reported_fcf 90,875.4 (OCF 133,220.0 - capex 42,344.6) - SBC 0 - interest income 10,594.7 = owner FCF 80,280.7 (18.9% of revenue). Of that, ~RMB 33.2bn was a working-capital inflow (inventories -39.8bn, receivables -16.9bn, payables +90.0bn per the FY2025 OCF reconciliation, 3750.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:12731-12736); ex-WC the FY0 owner FCF was ~RMB 47bn (11.1% of revenue), which is the base the component build is anchored to. The component-built year-1 owner FCF of ~RMB 56bn on RMB 623bn revenue (9.0%) is consistent with that ex-WC run-rate given the lower 2026 margin.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2030 average revenue growth (15/12/10/8). Equity CAGR (30.6% 2yr) is inflated by the RMB ~37bn May-2025 H-share IPO and FY2025's 42% profit jump at a peak margin; revenue 3yr CAGR (8.8%) is depressed by the FY2024 lithium-price deflation year (-9.7%). Neither is a clean forward proxy; 10% sits between them and is what the base driver path actually uses once the FY2026 pass-through surge laps.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 2yr CAGR 30.6% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 8.8% diverges >30%: equity growth is IPO-funded and margin-driven (FY2025 ROE 24.9%), not revenue-driven. FY2024 revenue fell 9.7% on lithium-carbonate price pass-through even as volumes rose; FY2026 revenue is rising ~47% partly for the opposite reason. Revenue CAGRs for this company are dominated by raw-material price pass-through and should be read alongside GWh volumes (FY2025 661 GWh, +39%).
historical_growth.notes: Source: FY2025 Annual Report Section IX Five-Year Financial Highlights (3750.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:15215-15261): revenue FY2021 130,355.8 / FY2022 328,594.0 / FY2023 400,917.0 / FY2024 362,012.6 / FY2025 423,701.8 (RMB m); diluted EPS 3.80 / 7.16 / 10.05 / 11.58 / 16.14. FY2020 is not in the filing, so there is no true 5-year CAGR; 4-year figures are given in their place. Shareholders' equity FY2023 197,708 -> FY2025 337,108. Owner FCF: FY2024 65,810 - 9,503 interest income - ~500 SBC = ~55.8bn; FY2025 80,280.7 -> +44% (one year only; FY2023 capex is not in the CSV). Owner-FCF growth is below reported-FCF growth (+38%) only marginally because SBC is immaterial; the gap between the two series is the interest-income strip, not SBC.

base.growth_note: Y1 FY2026 +47% is ~9 months actual (9M +56%) plus a Q4 of ~RMB 180bn. FY2027 +15% as the 2026 input-cost pass-through laps and pricing deflates against ~20-25% GWh growth (ESS +, EV mid-teens); decelerating to 3% by Y10 as global EV penetration matures.
base.margin_note: 21.8% Y1 is the FY2026E run-rate (H1 24.6%, Q3 ~19.7%) less 0.2pp for the bridged trading-asset return. 20.5% in FY2027-28 is roughly the Q3 FY2026 trough held, then a modest recovery to 21.0% as fixed-price ESS contracts signed before the 2025-26 input-cost rise roll off and overseas mix (31.4% GM vs 24.0% domestic) rises from 31% toward 40% of revenue. Deliberately below FY2024-25 (22.8%/25.6%).
base.capex_note: 9M FY2026 capex RMB 42.2bn (9.5% of revenue) with 321 GWh under construction; eases toward 7% as GWh growth slows. D&A rises from 5.5% (denominator inflated by the 2026 revenue surge) toward 6.5%, so terminal net investment is 0.5% of revenue at 3% growth.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 margin step-down (gross margin 26.3% -> 20.7% by Q3) is a re-basing, not a blip, but it stops around the Q3 level: the raw-material pass-through lag and the fixed-price ESS backlog signed before input costs rose work through by FY2027-28, and EBITDA margin settles at 20.5-21% -- the low end of the FY2022-25 range -- with the overseas mix shift (Hungary, Spain, Indonesia; overseas GM 31% vs 24% domestic) offsetting continued domestic price competition. Volume keeps growing: global share holds ~40% in EV and #1 in ESS, where shipments nearly doubled in H1 FY2026 and data-centre demand adds a vector uncorrelated with the auto cycle. Revenue growth decelerates from +47% (FY2026, mostly pass-through) to +15% then single digits as China NEV penetration (~55%) saturates. Capex eases from 9.5% to 7% of revenue as the 321 GWh under construction completes. US market access stays closed (1260H) but the EU local-content rules treat the Debrecen and Arnstadt plants as European. Net cash of RMB 147.5bn plus RMB 63bn of trading assets is added once; interest income is stripped from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Unit profit per Wh stabilises at ~RMB 0.11 while non-lithium input costs ease, so percentage margins recover toward 23-23.5% EBITDA by FY2029 as overseas revenue passes 40% of the mix at premium pricing, sodium-ion (Naxtra) and Shenxing fast-charge products carry a technology premium, and ESS pricing firms once the 2025-vintage fixed-price contracts roll off. Volume growth stays 20%+ through FY2028 on ESS (+AI data-centre power), European OEM design-wins on the Hungary ramp, and battery-swap network scale. Supplier-financed working capital resumes releasing cash (8% of the revenue increase). Global share drifts above 40%. The EU local-content regime lands favourably and the US overhang does not escalate to Entity List/OFAC.
scenario_narratives.bear: The compression is structural: Chinese cell overcapacity (BYD, EVE, CALB, Gotion) turns into a sustained price war, ESS pricing keeps falling faster than costs, and EBITDA margin settles at 16.5% -- roughly where a commodity-ish cell maker with CATL's scale lands (below FY2022's 20% GM trough). After the pass-through-inflated FY2026, revenue growth collapses to 3-5%: domestic NEV volumes plateau as trade-in subsidies lapse, the EU 'Made in Europe' thresholds disadvantage Chinese-owned cells even from Hungary, and the US designation escalates (UFLPA/Entity List), closing US-exposed OEM programmes (Ford licensing). Working capital turns into a drag (-5% of revenue growth) as receivables and inventory outgrow supplier financing, as they did in 9M FY2026. Capex cannot fall as fast as growth because overseas plants are committed. The business remains solidly profitable and net cash -- this is a margin-and-growth bear, not a solvency bear.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the margin trend is three quarters old and still worsening, the sector-overcapacity risk is flagged by management itself, and the US/EU regulatory axes are binary and outside CATL's control; it stays at 25% rather than higher because the balance sheet is net cash RMB 147bn, volumes are still growing ~40%, and the bear is a margin case, not a solvency case. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (input costs easing, ESS pricing firming, favourable EU/US outcomes) at the same time. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CATL is valued as a scaled, net-cash, cyclical manufacturer whose 2026 margin re-basing is taken as the new normal rather than reversed. The value lives in volume growth at a 20-21% EBITDA margin with capex intensity falling as the capacity build completes; the FY2025 25.6% margin and the FY2025 RMB 33bn working-capital windfall are explicitly not carried forward. Risk is charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, once, at a single CNY-built 9.5% discount rate. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF (cyclical), and the 10-year horizon is needed because capex intensity and D&A are still converging in year 5.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 6-7% of base-case value; the bear's 16.5% versus the base's 21% is the dominant spread

Growth after FY2026 is a volume-versus-price judgment: 2026 revenue is inflated by raw-material pass-through, and a 2027 reversal (cost deflation passed back to OEMs) could make reported revenue growth near zero while GWh still grow 20%
Working-capital sign: FY2025 released RMB 33bn, 9M FY2026 consumed RMB 25bn; the base takes zero credit but a sustained reversal of supplier financing would cut interim FCF materially
Regulatory binaries: US 1260H escalation to Entity List/OFAC, EU local-content thresholds that do not recognise Hungary/Germany production, and lapsing Chinese NEV trade-in subsidies

Bridge items: RMB 63bn trading financial assets added at carrying value; RMB 72.8bn equity investments excluded (their income stays in EBITDA); NCI charged via a 6% leakage, not at book -- each is a stated choice a reader may reverse
Quote basis: the H-share trades at a ~31% premium to the A-share; HKD per-share values are CNY values x 1.1735, so the same intrinsic value implies very different upside on the two listings
